transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23 15:19 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Helios Head of Data), Nikhil Gupta (Helios ML Eng), Sara Thompson (Helios Security Lead)

Auto-summary (auto): Intro, requirements, questions on context length and multilingual, tool-calling demo ask, security checklist and next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate it. quick round of intros and then we'll jump into what you're trying to solve at Helios.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Lena): hi, lena here, head of data, we run chat and assisted shopping flows across web and mobile, looking to replace a brittle rule-based agent and want an LLM backend that can do product lookups and context-aware recommendations across 3 languages.
00:27 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): hey i'm nikhil, ml, mostly focused on latency and cost per request, we do a lot of long threads — ticket histories sometimes hit 25k tokens, some go higher.
00:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): got it, long histories and multilingual. diego do you want to frame how redwood thinks about model selection for this?
00:45 Speaker 4 (Diego): yeah thanks. at a high level we pick models based on three axes: quality for your prompts and domain, cost/latency on your expected throughput, and ops constraints — meaning whether you want hosted, dedicated reserved pools, or private vpc/on-prem. for long context we look at optimized models that support 32k or 64k token windows and also, importantly, runtime behaviors like kv cache and prefix caching to reduce re-compute.
01:08 Speaker 2 (Lena): when you say prefix caching, is that like a session cache? we have many repeat prefixes because customers often ask follow-ups.
01:15 Speaker 4 (Diego): exactly — automatic prefix caching will reuse cached KV state for identical conversation prefixes. reduces per-token work. we also support continuous batching and can tune autoscale to keep latency below your SLO while minimizing cost.
01:29 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): what's the practical difference between hosted and dedicated for throughput? if we have spikes around sales events — black friday style — do we get throttled on hosted?
01:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): hosted is typically best for fast onboarding and pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with SLA — you can configure burst policies for events. private is when you need VPC or on-prem for compliance.
01:52 Speaker 5 (Sara): on compliance, we need to know about encryption at rest and key mgmt — we use a cloud KMS and some customers require HSM-backed keys. do you support that on private?
02:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes, private deploys can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we maintain audit logs. hosted supports encryption and SOC 2 but not customer-managed HSM unless you move to private. we'll share the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram.
02:20 Speaker 2 (Lena): thanks. model-wise, we're leaning open-source for cost control. which models are you recommending for long-context multilingual tool-calling?
02:30 Speaker 4 (Diego): for open models, we've seen good results with the newer family that have 32k windows — some forks of Llama-like models and newer M-models. quality varies by language; often for Japanese we want a model that was trained with multi-lingual corpora. another axis is quantization: 8-bit and 4-bit options reduce memory and cost but sometimes hit quality for tool-calling when you need strict formatting.
02:53 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): can you elaborate on tool-calling? we need reliable structured outputs to call our product catalog service — ideally function-calling or structured JSON with schema validation.
03:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): we support tool-calling primitives: you can register tools/endpoints, define function schemas, and the runtime will do structured outputs and can stream events when the model calls a tool. we also provide post-call validation hooks so your service can confirm payloads and reject malformed requests. caveat: some quantized models are less deterministic with exact JSON formatting; we can tune prompts and use constrained generation to improve reliability.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Lena): hmm, we also do multilingual — English, French, Japanese — any particular model that balances high quality across those three?
03:40 Speaker 4 (Diego): typically ensembles or fallback routing helps: route English requests to a higher-accuracy English-specialized model and French/Japanese to multilingual variants. redwood routing policies can do region/language-based routing and fallback to hosted or lower-cost variants when needed.
03:55 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): latency targets — we're aiming for sub-300ms 95p for single-turn product calls, is that feasible?
04:03 Speaker 4 (Diego): for small context and optimized kernels you can hit that in dedicated environments. hosted can get close depending on model size and batching; dedicated with pinned models and instance types will be more predictable.
04:15 Speaker 5 (Sara): auditability is critical — request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns?
04:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, console has tracing hooks and you can get token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. for private we can emit logs to your SIEM.
04:32 Speaker 2 (Lena): what's the perf delta between 32k and 64k context? do models slow down linearly?
04:40 Speaker 4 (Diego): not exactly linear — runtime kernel selection and attention optimizations matter. beyond some lengths we see quadratic-like slowdowns if not using locality-optimized attention. the runtime will pick optimized kernels and we recommend quantized weights plus KV caching to keep tail latency reasonable.
05:00 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): for our ticket histories we mostly need 32k; maybe occasional 48k. what's the cost trade-off to support up to 64k in dedicated?
05:10 Speaker 4 (Diego): supporting 64k often requires larger memory footprint or model sharding across GPUs, which increases infra cost. we can present a cost matrix — model vram, vcpu, expected tokens per request, and estimated $/1000 requests.
05:24 Speaker 2 (Lena): can we run a small POC: two models, one smaller 32k-optimized, one larger 64k-optimized, run them against 1000 sample conversations and measure latency, hallucination rate, tool-calling reliability?
05:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): absolutely. diego can scope that. we'll run hosted bench first for quick turnaround and then optionally move to dedicated.
05:43 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): hosted bench — any privacy concerns? samples will include PII. we need to be sure hosted won't persist data beyond the bench.
05:52 Speaker 4 (Diego): we can set bench runs to avoid persistent logs and redact/obfuscate during testing. for production with PII, we recommend dedicated or private depending on your retention and audit requirements.
06:05 Speaker 5 (Sara): our legal team will also ask about data residency — some EU customer data must stay in EU. are multi-region private deployments supported?
06:12 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes, we support region affinity and private control plane can be deployed in customer region or cloud region of choice. for hosted, we have EU regions; for strict residency we recommend private.
06:26 Speaker 2 (Lena): switching gears — what about embeddings and retrieval? we currently use a vector DB and about 1.2M docs, need embedding throughput and cost estimates.
06:35 Speaker 4 (Diego): embeddings are supported; we can batch-create and provide lineage. we also offer embedding caching and suggestion on quantization for index size reduction. for 1.2M docs we typically recommend an offline embedding pipeline plus incremental updates.
06:50 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): does the runtime support streaming token outputs while doing tool-calls? we want progressive UI updates.
06:58 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes streaming is supported; when tool-calling we can provide interleaved events: partial text, then call event, then resumed text. works well for UI.
07:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick check on stakeholders and timeline — who's the decision maker and what's the desired timeline?
07:16 Speaker 2 (Lena): we're piloting now, decision maker is the VP product and CTO. timeline — pilot in Q3, production in Q4 if pilot succeeds.
07:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): great; pilot in Q3 — we'll prioritize a hosted bench that can be migrated to dedicated.
07:29 Speaker 2 (Lena): budget-wise, we prefer predictable monthly for the pilot, but open to usage if cost benefits are clear.
07:36 Speaker 4 (Diego): we'll propose both: pay-as-you-go estimate for hosted and a reserved-dedicated ballpark.
07:42 Speaker 5 (Sara): one more security question — do you support SAML SSO, RBAC, and per-route access controls?
07:50 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes SAML + SCIM, RBAC, and route-level policies are supported, plus audit logs. per-route encryption keys are available on private.
07:59 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): what about model updates and rollback? we need canarying and quick rollback in case of regressions.
08:06 Speaker 4 (Diego): redwood console supports rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to older model variants. we also integrate with your CI to deploy eval prompt sets and regression alerts.
08:20 Speaker 2 (Lena): curious about hallucination checks — do you have an eval harness?
08:26 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes, we have evals tied to prompt sets, regression alerts, and quality thresholds that can gate rollouts. you can run automated scoring for hallucination and precision on your dataset.
08:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): sounds like we have enough to scope a POC. diego, suggested bench configuration?
08:46 Speaker 4 (Diego): propose two models: Model A — 32k open-model tuned for multilingual with quantization at 8-bit; Model B — 64k larger model with more parameters, lightly quantized. tests: latency, 95p tail, token cost, tool-calling success rate (schema-valid JSON), multilingual quality (EN/FR/JP). run on hosted infra first for 2-3 days, then move Model A onto a small dedicated pool for steady-state sim.
09:10 Speaker 2 (Lena): timeline works. about pricing for dedicated, any commitments? we prefer monthly reserved.
09:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): we do monthly and annual reserved tiers; we'll include a committed option in pricing.
09:23 Speaker 5 (Sara): for SOC2 and security questionnaire, we'll need answers in a week.
09:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll share SOC2 and fill the questionnaire; diego you'll attach the architecture diagram for private.
09:34 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes i'll attach private deployment diagram and notes about KMS/HSM integration.
09:39 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): small technical Q — does redwood support KV cache eviction policies and per-session TTLs? our sessions can be long-lived and we need to expire old context.
09:49 Speaker 4 (Diego): yes, you can set TTLs on session caches and configure eviction strategies; we also expose metrics for cache hit rates.
09:58 Speaker 2 (Lena): any gotchas for multilingual tokenization and cost — e.g., Japanese tokenizes differently and affects token counts?
10:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): correct — tokenization impacts cost. some multilingual models use subword tokenizers more efficient for certain languages. we'll estimate tokenization delta in the perf matrix.
10:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok final recap before next steps — lena, nikhil, sara, does this match your expectations?
10:22 Speaker 2 (Lena): yep, pilot, hosted benches, security docs, and possible dedicated for Q4.
10:27 Speaker 5 (Sara): yes we'll send security questionnaire and residency constraints.
10:30 Speaker 3 (Nikhil): i'll assemble sample conversations and load.
10:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. next steps: 1) we'll send model perf + pricing spreadsheet; 2) diego runs hosted benchmark with your samples; 3) share SOC2 + private architecture diagrams; 4) schedule follow-up in one week.
10:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

(end of recording)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings — e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as "kay V cache", model family names obfuscated. References: redwood docs link to model catalog (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/models) and security packet (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2).

Explicit next meeting: proposed 2026-07-30 for initial bench results (to be confirmed).
